blocks.etymology: From clank + -er, onomatopoeic. The sense meaning "robot" appears in science fiction at least as early as 1958. Its broader popular use increased on social media beginning around 2024, due to the AI boom. In this wave of usage, it was especially influenced by the word's appearance in the Star Wars franchise, particularly the 2005 video game Star Wars: Republic Commando. In Star Wars, the term was used towards B1-series battle droids, which were humanoid robots that were manufactured for the sole purpose of fighting in armed conflicts. Their nickname of "clanker" stems from the fact that they would frequently make clanking noises any time they moved around due to being cheaply mass-produced.

blocks.etymology: From Late Latin vulnerābilis (“injurious, wounding”), from Latin vulnerō (“to wound”).

senses.definition: Easily hurt, damaged, or attacked physically or emotionally.

examples.en: Old people are especially vulnerable to the flu in winter.
examples.vi: Người già đặc biệt dễ bị tổn thương trước bệnh cúm vào mùa đông.

examples.en: Small businesses are vulnerable during an economic crisis.
examples.vi: Các doanh nghiệp nhỏ rất dễ bị tổn thương trong thời kỳ khủng hoảng kinh tế.

senses.vi: dễ bị tổn thương; dễ bị tấn công

senses.definition: Willing to show open feelings and risk being hurt emotionally.

examples.en: It takes courage to be completely vulnerable with another person.
examples.vi: Cần có sự can đảm để hoàn toàn mở lòng với một người khác.

senses.definition: Weak and open to cyber attacks or computer viruses.

examples.en: Outdated software makes your computer vulnerable to online hackers.
examples.vi: Phần mềm lỗi thời khiến máy tính của bạn dễ bị tin tặc tấn công.

senses.vi: dễ bị xâm nhập; có lỗ hổng bảo mật

vi_block: Có thể bị tổn thương; có thể bị tấn công, công kích được; có chỗ yếu, có nhược điểm.

examples: You are vulnerable to be bullied by someone at school.
wiktionary.gloss: More or most likely to be exposed to the chance of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.

examples: It's okay to get vulnerable every now and again.
wiktionary.gloss: Open to disclosing one's inner thoughts and feelings, acting in spite of one's instinct to self-preservation.

examples: a vulnerable PC with no antivirus software
wiktionary.gloss: More likely to be exposed to malicious programs or viruses.

examples: Welsh is merely a vulnerable language, but Irish and Scottish Gaelic are definitely endangered.
wiktionary.gloss: at moderate risk of extinction though not quite endangered.

tatoeba.en: There is an whole industry based entirely on preying upon financially vulnerable individuals.
